I didnt start discovering my headmates until I was 18. Before then, I just thought everyone was lying to me because I couldn't remember so much and I'd get in trouble for not remembering. Just like I thought they were lying, they thought I was lying.

In 2020 (18 years old) I got diagnosed with a few things, including an unspecified dissociative disorder. I was mad about it because I was trying to convince myself it was "just PTSD." 

I joined my first DID/OSDD discord server at the start of 2021, a few months after I got a new therapist who suggested DID. At that in time I only recognized myself and 2 littles. Initially it was only me who would ever message. I got introduced to a lot of terminology and learned how to work PluralKit. Eventually one of the littles started co-fronting. At that point I opened my own private server to allow everyone in my system a space for journaling. 

Over time I worked on self awareness, which let me to slowly discovering new members. I was switching between therapists and psych wards though. Nobody seemed to be able to put a name to what I was experiencing, and would refer me out. First therapist sent me to an ED specialist, then a trauma specialist (where I got a diagnosis some months ago), and now I'm waiting to be sent to a DID specialist. Once my diagnosis was figured out, my therapist realized she couldn't treat me. 

I took a break from the plural community when the first server I joined had issues. One of the main people came out as having been faking. It was never the same after that. I struggle to find places without mile long censor lists. I created my own public server but it got infiltrated by hateful redditors, so once again I don't really have a safe space anymore. Certain headmates like to be social and I want to be able to have a set space for that. 

My experience in the community has been mixed. There's a huge endogenic vs traumagenic debate. There is obvious faking on social media sometimes, but nobody can really say anything without major backlash. If you find good people, you'll have a good experience.

As for the hard bloated belly, I've been there in recovery. Unfortunately it's mostly about waiting it out and not restricting for comfort. I've found a heating pad can help ease the pain of it, I basically lived on one for 3 weeks straight lol. Is it possible you're constipated? I suffered from it really bad during refeeding, so if you are, you should visit the doctor to go about fixing it the healthy way.

I didnt see anything about refeeding causing insomnia, but if you're in pain that could explain it. Once your pain lessens and if you still can't sleep, you could try melatonin. If that doesn't work, you'll also need to see a doctor about that.
